clue.text: New Orleans fury with Londoner

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the place name's letters are reworked into a fresh order

blocks.note: the city name taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A storm of rage in New Orleans, apparently involving a visitor from London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' reads as the American city, but 'New' is the signal and only Orleans is shuffled. A Sloane Ranger is a stereotypical posh young Londoner from around Sloane Square in Chelsea.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sloane Ranger is an upper-class, fashionable young person living in west London, so the term names a particular kind of city resident.

clue.text: Hurry up and be smartly dressed

explanation.surface: An instruction to rush and also turn up looking well groomed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an order to be quick and alert, while its literal reading means presenting a crisp, stylish appearance.

clue.text: Current + current + current divided by current? That's not basic!

indicators.note: a thing divided by something has that something sitting in its middle, splitting it in two

blocks.note: AC is alternating current
I is the physics symbol for electric current
DC is direct current
the physics symbol for current again

explanation.surface: A sum written like a physics equation, with the solver told this is no elementary problem.
explanation.walkthrough: AC + I + D(I)C gives ACIDIC. 'Not basic' sounds like 'not easy', but in chemistry basic means alkaline.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, a base is the opposite of an acid, so a substance that is not alkaline has a pH below seven.

the opening letter of the word

clue.text: Vague and murky blue adopted by us for Christian Dior

clue.text: Selfish person remains so after losing heart

setter's reading: drop the middle letter of the answer and what is left is still a word for a selfish person

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed individual who stays self-absorbed even when disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the central T of EGOTIST and you get EGOIST, another word for a selfish person, so it remains so.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is someone excessively absorbed in themselves and their own importance, a standard synonym for a self-centred individual.

clue.text: Loud bling

second meaning: a pierced lobe holding showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Showy, gaudy jewellery of the kind worn to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud bling' reads as flashy jewellery; the two words are separate meanings. Bling is slang for ostentatious jewellery.

clue.text: Question old style chef, ultimately about cheese

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old style chef' looks like a description of a cook; it only supplies three final letters, DE(BRIE)F.

clue.text: Rue le Frère: some need relocation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rue' poses as the French word for street, but it is the English verb meaning to regret.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it bitterly, which is the same as experiencing contrition or sorrow over it.

taken as written

explanation.surface: The Soviet Union in disarray during a journey that allowed something risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'En route' reads as the familiar phrase for on the way, but the two words must be split: 'en' is French for in and acts as the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian roulette is the deadly game of spinning a revolver loaded with one bullet and pulling the trigger at one's own head.

clue.text: Somewhat disciplinarian regressive state

blocks.note: found running through the final letters of the word

clue.text: Do what's essential to infiltrate old-fashioned right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb of the command, but it is the definition in the sense 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is to be good enough, just as something that will do is acceptable or satisfactory.

clue.text: Setter is going to get introduced to one fruit or another

explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small green husked fruit used in Mexican cooking, a different fruit from the one in the wordplay.

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the final letter of the word

clue.text: Preacher's type of animism is free of sin

blocks.note: taken as written
these letters are removed

explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and often delivers the Friday sermon, so he is a religious leader who preaches.

the answer to 3 Down
